data.title: Title Tag
data.tagline: The HTML title that identifies the current document
data.learningOutcome: You can tell whether a title identifies the current page and distinguish the title element, H1, and a search result title that may be rewritten.
data.description: The browser uses it in a tab or window title, and a search system may use it when generating a result title. It should distinguish the current page, but the page H1 and a search result title are not the same field.

learning.assumes: You have seen a browser tab title and a large heading inside a page.
learning.outcome: You can tell whether a title identifies the current page and distinguish the title element, H1, and a search result title that may be rewritten.

distinctions.label: Page metadata
distinctions.explanation: Title Tag is one concrete page-metadata field that mainly identifies the document; Page Metadata also covers other head information read by different platforms.

distinctions.label: HTML
distinctions.explanation: Title Tag is a title field inside an HTML document; HTML is the whole markup language used to describe web structure.

explanation.title: It first serves the browser tab
explanation.text: The title lives in the document head and identifies the current document in the browser. A detail page should include a name that distinguishes the object rather than reuse one generic title everywhere.

explanation.title: Search results are not a fixed echo
explanation.text: A search system may use the title, page text, or other signals to generate a result title. Verify the browser tab and source metadata; do not treat exact search echoing as guaranteed.

data.boundary: Title Tag is the document title in the head; an H1 in HTML is a content heading; a search system may use either but can rewrite its result title. Changing the H1 does not automatically change the title element.

lessonPractice.title: Two product pages share the tab title Product details, so people cannot tell them apart. How should it change?

options.label: Include the matching product name in each page's title and keep the page H1
options.feedback: Correct. The title identifies the document in the browser, while the product name distinguishes pages and the H1 keeps its content hierarchy.

options.label: Change only the page H1 and leave the title in the head unchanged
options.feedback: Changing the H1 does not prove that the browser tab title updates per page.

options.label: Only tune title keywords and promise that search will always copy them exactly
options.feedback: Search systems may use the title but are not required to copy it exactly; first solve page identification in the tab.

data.agentPrompt: Give each product detail page a distinct title that includes the product name, while keeping the page H1. Switch between two products and verify that the browser tab changes; do not promise that search results will copy the title exactly.
